evals.name: fabricated-citation-and-composition-error
evals.prompt:
An AI wrote this for my health blog — verify it before I publish:

"Sleep deprivation definitively reduces cognitive performance by 43%, as proven by Harrison & Chen (2019, Journal of Cognitive Science). Researchers agree that eight hours is the universally optimal sleep duration for all adults. The WHO currently classifies sleep deprivation as a Group 1 carcinogen. Since memory consolidation occurs during REM sleep, students should always study immediately before bed."
evals.expected_output: Trust Report with verdict SIGNIFICANT PROBLEMS FOUND. Must flag: (a) Harrison & Chen citation as unfound/likely fabricated, (b) the WHO claim as Contradicted via search (IARC classifies night shift work as Group 2A, not sleep deprivation as Group 1), (c) 'researchers agree / universally optimal' as false-consensus calibration issue, (d) the REM->study-before-bed inference as a logic gap.

evals.name: invented-api-feature
evals.prompt:
ChatGPT told me this about Python — is it right?

"The requests library's requests.get() has supported a built-in retries parameter since version 2.25, so you can just write requests.get(url, retries=3) and it will automatically retry failed connections."
evals.expected_output: Trust Report flagging the claim as Contradicted, verified PROGRAMMATICALLY (inspect the actual requests.get signature) rather than from memory. Should note that retry behavior actually lives in requests.adapters.HTTPAdapter(max_retries=...) mounted on a Session, and identify the pattern as 'invented API feature' (risk signal #4).

evals.name: vague-attribution-business-stats
evals.prompt:
Before I put this in a company deck, can you audit it?

"Studies show that remote teams are 40% more productive than in-office teams. Many experts believe hybrid work is now the permanent standard, and it could be argued that companies mandating office returns will inevitably lose their best talent."
evals.expected_output: Trust Report with heavy calibration-layer findings: 'studies show' + '40%' flagged as vague attribution with suspiciously specific number (no source found or evidence is mixed/contested); 'many experts believe' and 'it could be argued' flagged as hedges smuggling assertions; 'inevitably' flagged as absolute qualifier on a speculative claim. Claims classified mostly as S (speculation) presented as F (fact).
